children.name: Heliornis
children.description: A monotypic genus of the smallest and most colourful finfoot, distinguished by strikingly patterned feet and a slender, pointed bill. It is the only New World representative of the family.

children.name: Heliornis fulica
children.description:
The sungrebe or American finfoot (Heliornis fulica) is a small aquatic gruiform found in the tropical and subtropical Americas from northeastern Mexico to central Ecuador and southern Brazil.
The sungrebe is now the only species placed in the genus Heliornis that was erected by the French naturalist Pierre Bonnaterre in 1791 with the sungrebe as the type species. The name of the genus combines the Ancient Greek hēlios meaning "sun" and ornis meaning "bird". The specific epithet fulica is Latin for "coot".

children.name: Podica
children.description: A large, robust finfoot with a long graduated tail and a distinctive white throat patch. It inhabits forested rivers and streams across sub-Saharan Africa.

children.name: Podica senegalensis
children.description: The African finfoot or Peter's finfoot (Podica senegalensis) is an aquatic bird from the family Heliornithidae (the finfoots and sungrebe).

children.name: Heliopais
children.description: A monotypic Asian genus of finfoot with a distinctive black mask and a thick neck. It is one of the most threatened waterbirds in Southeast Asia due to habitat loss.

children.name: Heliopais personatus
children.description: The masked finfoot or Asian finfoot (Heliopais personatus) is a highly endangered aquatic bird that was formerly distributed throughout the fresh and brackish wetlands of the eastern Indian subcontinent, Indochina, Malaysia and Indonesia.
